question: Should `tools.exec.denylist` become a supported core security guardrail whose STOP rules apply to ordinary full/off execution but remain bypassable by explicitly authorized elevated-full execution?
rationale: This adds persistent configuration and changes approval precedence across privileged execution hosts; tests cannot determine whether elevated-full is intended to override an operator-authored STOP rule.

options.title: Approve the break-glass contract
options.body: Accept the single-owner config design and elevated-full exception after the docs defect and integrated macOS proof are resolved.

options.title: Make STOP rules absolute
options.body: Require denylist approval even for elevated-full execution and update gateway, node, macOS, tests, and docs accordingly.

options.title: Do not add the core surface
options.body: Close or redesign the feature if maintainers do not want another persistent exec-policy configuration contract.

recommendation.title: Approve the break-glass contract
recommendation.body: Accept the single-owner config design and elevated-full exception after the docs defect and integrated macOS proof are resolved.

likelyOwner.reason: The available feature history and PR discussion point to steipete as the strongest owner for exec-policy and security-boundary decisions.
